full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, briefly, are that the petitioners as plaintiff's filed Title Suit No. 195 of 2000 in the court of Assistant Judge, Meherpur impleading the opposite parties as defendants for declaration of title and cancellation of deed Nos. 2829 and 2830 dated 3-4-2000 as void, collusive without consideration. The plaintiffs' case in short is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and Defendants Siratul Mondol was the inhabitant of West Bengal. Later on, Siratul Mondol used to live in village Babupur, District-Meherpur, who purchased 7.49 acre of land from the disputed SA Khatian No. 92 by sale deed No. 3010 dated 7-6-1962 and mutated his name and obtained dakhilas. Thereafter, Siratul Mondol sold 24 decimal of land to defendant No, 6 Anwara Khatun and subsequently handed over possession to her. After selling of the said land, Siratul Mondol had rest 7.25 acres of land, who did not exchange his land with land of West Bengal in lieu of that he gifted his land measuring 7.25 acres to his 4 (four) sons Rofezuddin, Mofezuddin, Harunur Rashid and Golam Hossain and left for West Bengal. Siratul Mondol gave marriage to his 3 (three) daughters namely Janera Khatun, Abironnesa and Joigon Biwi in West Bengal and they lived with their husband's house. Thereafter, Siratul Mondol died in West Beneal and later on his wife died. Siratul Mondol died leaving behind 4 (four) sons in Bangladesh and 3 (three) daughters in India. Father of the plaintiff No. 3 got land from his father and gifted to his daughter Ponka Nesa and lived in his house situated in West Bengal. The land of India owned by Siratul Mondol was possessed and enjoyed by his 3 (three) daughters. The disputed land was neither owned nor possessed by the defendant Nos. 2-3 and 5. The plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 have been owned and possessed 1.81 acres of land from their father and plaintiff No. 3 owned and possessed 1.81. acres of land from her father Mofezuddin. The defendant No. 1 owned and possessed 1.81 acres land by meets and bounds. Daughters of the Siratul Mondol never came in the then East Pakistan and the defendant Nos. 2-5 lived in West. Bengal for many years. In this background very recent the defendant No. 1 demanded title and interest in favor of the defendant No. 2-3 and he bought the property in their names. Actually the defendant Nos. 2-3 never came in Bangladesh and became inhabitant of Babupur village. The plaintiff Nos. 1-2 on search in the Meherpur Sub-Registry office found that on 3-4-2000 the defendant No. 1 executed and registered 2 (two) different deeds being No. 2829 and 2830 with the help of their men. The defendant No. 1 with a view to harass the plaintiff created 2 (two) fake and fabricated deeds in the name of the defendant No. 2 and 3. The defendant No. 2 and 3 are the inhabitants of India and they never came in Bangladesh and they did not execute and register any deeds in favor of the defendant No. 1. They never present in the Meherpur Sub-Registry office and received any consideration amount as land value. The defendant No. 1 long after the filing of this suit fabricated another deed as executed in the name of the Defendant Nos. 2 and 3 again on 13-1-2002 being deed No. 576 registered in the office of the Meherpur Sub-Registry Office and in support of the said deed dated 13-1-2002 made an affidavit. Actually the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 never came in Bangladesh and registered deed in their names. The plaintiff collected certified copy of the said forged deeds dated 4-5-2000 and hence, the suit. 

 3. The opposite party No.1 as defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material averments made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the disputed land under RS Khatian No. 260 was originally belonged to Siratul Mondol and others. Siratul Mondol died leaving behind 4 (four) sons named Rokuddin, Mofezuddin, Harunur Rashid, Golam Hossain and 3 (three) daughters named Joygun, Janera and Abiron out of them each son got 1.31 acre of land and each daughter got 65 decimal of land. During owning and possessing the same in ejmali Janera and Abiron on 3-4-2000 transferred 90.25 decimals of land by sale deed No. 2829 and 31.80 decimal of land by sale deed No. 2830 to defendant No. 1. Thereafter, the plaintiff refused to acknowledge the above mentioned deeds and thereafter, the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 executed sale deed No. 576 on 13-1-2002 measuring 131.50 decimals of !and in favor of the defendant No. 1 and executed an Affidavit on 14-1-2002 in connection with the above mentioned deeds before the Meherpur Notary Public Office. The father of the plaintiff never gifted the disputed land to the plaintiffs. Deed Nos. 2829 and 2830 dated 3-4-2000 is not illegal, fabricated, fake or without consideration. The plaintiffs have no right, tide and possession over the land of deeds dated 3-4-2000. The defendants and plaintiffs owing and possessing the disputed land by inheritance and purchase in ejmali. The plaintiffs filed the suit on false averments and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
